To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the US market influences Asian markets in terms of price level, Asian markets influence the US market in terms of price volatility, and both markets influence each other in terms of trading volume.

(1) the Asian markets do not influence the US market; (2) the US market influences the Asian markets, and the influence is stronger on the absolute returns than on returns themselves, and is stronger in volatility than in returns; and (3) the Asian markets influence each other, and the influence runs from the more volatile market to the more quiet one.

(1) there are strong spillovers in return volatility from Asia to the United States; (2) there are strong cross border spillover effects in returns, but only weak ones in trading volumes; (3) the 1997 Asian financial crisis seems to have made Asian markets more sensitive to news from the US.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic relation between stock index returns, trading volume, and return volatility in eight major Asian markets and the USA, and the spillovers between these markets.
the dynamic relationship between returns, trading volume, and volatility in the Asian financial markets.
the dynamics of the financial markets, which is an important issue, as the dynamics of the market are crucial for the functioning of the economy as a whole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the financial market is not a random walk.
the Asian markets, in particular the Korean market, are more volatile, less efficient, more susceptible to foreign news, and more susceptible to foreign trading volume than the US markets.
Asian markets are more sensitive to US news, and the US market to Asian news, but the US market is more volatile than the Asian markets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Asian financial crisis of 1997-98 was a result of a combination of factors, including a large current account deficit and a large foreign debt, which were aggravated by a sudden loss of confidence among foreign investors.
the Asian crisis of 1997-1998 had a profound impact on financial markets, not only in Asia, but also in the US.
the Asian markets are more integrated with the US market than with the Asian markets themselves.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Asian markets, especially those with higher levels of development, have been increasingly influenced by shocks in the US market, and this influence is not limited to returns, but extends to volatility and volume as well.
the Asian financial crisis was a result of an interaction between the US market, which was the source of the shock and the Asian markets, where the shock was amplified and propagated.
the Asian markets have become much more integrated with the US market, and this is especially true since the Asian crisis.
